name: Thomas
overview: Thomas was a male disciple of the Messiah and one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus Christ. He is specifically identified in Matthew 10:3 as one of the Twelve, highlighting his role as a close follower and representative of Christ during His earthly ministry.
namesAndTitles: Thomas is the primary name used for this disciple, with no specific meaning provided in the facts. He is also known by the name Didymus, as recorded in John 11:16. Both names are proper names given by people and do not carry divine naming significance in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Thomas's relationship as a disciple and apostle of YHVH (Jesus Christ), explicitly stated in Matthew 10:3. Beyond this, there are no family relationships documented for Thomas in the given facts.
scriptureSignificance: Thomas holds significance as one of the twelve apostles, chosen personally by Jesus to be His close followers and messengers. His inclusion among the Twelve underscores his role in the foundational group that witnessed Jesus’ ministry and carried forward the gospel message. This status as a disciple and apostle marks him as an important figure in the early Christian community.
